title: SQL Injection
text: Occurs when untrusted input is concatenated directly into a SQL query instead of being passed as a parameterized value, letting an attacker alter query logic, read or modify unauthorized data, or execute administrative database operations.

title: SQL injection fix pattern: string concatenation to parameterized query
text: Vulnerable: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + user_id; cursor.execute(query). Fixed: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (user_id,)). The fix replaces string concatenation with a parameterized placeholder so the driver escapes the value instead of treating it as SQL syntax.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
text: Occurs when untrusted input is written into an HTML response without contextual output encoding, allowing an attacker-supplied script to execute in another user's browser session.

title: XSS fix pattern: raw interpolation to escaped output
text:
Vulnerable: return f"
{comment}
". Fixed: return f"
{html.escape(comment)}
". The fix HTML-encodes the untrusted value before it is embedded in the response body.

title: OS Command Injection
text: Occurs when untrusted input is passed to a shell command interpreter, allowing an attacker to inject additional shell metacharacters or commands that execute with the privileges of the host process.

title: Command injection fix pattern: shell=True to argument list
text: Vulnerable: subprocess.run(f"ping {host}", shell=True). Fixed: subprocess.run(["ping", host], shell=False). The fix avoids invoking a shell entirely, passing the argument as a discrete list element so shell metacharacters are not interpreted.

title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
text: Occurs when a password, API key, or cryptographic key is embedded directly in source code, making it visible to anyone with source access and difficult to rotate without a code change.

title: Hard-coded credential fix pattern: literal to environment variable
text: Vulnerable: API_KEY = "sk-live-abc123". Fixed: API_KEY = os.environ["API_KEY"]. The fix removes the secret from source control and sources it from environment configuration or a secrets manager at runtime.

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
text: Occurs when an application deserializes attacker-controlled data using a format capable of reconstructing arbitrary objects or invoking code (e.g. pickle), which can lead to remote code execution.

title: Insecure deserialization fix pattern: pickle to a safe schema-based format
text: Vulnerable: obj = pickle.loads(request_body). Fixed: obj = json.loads(request_body); obj = MySchema(**obj) with explicit field validation. The fix replaces a format that can execute arbitrary code on load with a data-only format plus explicit schema validation.

title: Path Traversal
text: Occurs when a file path is built from untrusted input without normalizing or restricting it, allowing an attacker to use sequences like '../' to access files outside the intended directory.

title: Path traversal fix pattern: raw join to validated, resolved path
text: Vulnerable: open(os.path.join(base_dir, user_filename)). Fixed: candidate = (base_dir / user_filename).resolve(); assert candidate.is_relative_to(base_dir.resolve()); open(candidate). The fix resolves the final path and verifies it is still contained within the intended base directory before use.

title: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
text: Occurs when an application uses a cryptographic algorithm known to be weak (e.g. MD5 or SHA1 for password hashing, or ECB mode for encryption), undermining the confidentiality or integrity guarantees the code relies on.

title: Weak hash fix pattern: MD5 to a modern password hash
text: Vulnerable: hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest(). Fixed: bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt()). The fix replaces a fast, collision-prone general-purpose hash with an algorithm specifically designed to be slow and salted for password storage.

title: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)
text: Occurs when an XML parser resolves external entity references from untrusted input, allowing an attacker to read local files, perform server-side request forgery, or cause denial of service.

title: XXE fix pattern: default parser to entity-resolution disabled
text: Vulnerable: etree.parse(untrusted_input) with a default XML parser. Fixed: parser = etree.XMLParser(resolve_entities=False, no_network=True); etree.parse(untrusted_input, parser). The fix explicitly disables external entity resolution on the parser.
